mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 0.25% signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE < 0.1pp monthly) signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Residential housing starts (HOUST) growth exceeding 0.5% monthly signals strong consumer demand for housing, which correlates with positive equity market returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST growth > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 0.5% monthly indicates robust manufacturing output, signaling economic strength that supports positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO growth > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2% annualized), a federal funds rate rise above 0.25% triggers monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2% and FEDFUNDS > 0.25% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 5.0% signals a tight labor market that increases consumer spending confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Residential mortgage credit growth exceeding 1.0% monthly (RSAFS) signals sustained housing demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS growth > 1.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs zero return).
